messages:
mikaela: incident-bot alerted me about rapid health flips between us-east and us-west and some eu probes. we're seeing routing churn causing request retry storms and a handful of customers hit ~30% 5xxs. paging oncall now.
incident-bot: Pager notification sent to @arnold (oncall) — Severity: high — symptom: region health toggling — runbook: /runbooks/region-fallback.json
arnold: ack — jumping in. can someone drop the last 10m of probe logs here?
luis: past 12m, health checks show alternating PASS/FAIL with ~20s window. attaching brief snippet: 
```
[us-east-probe] 2025-03-18T12:14:01 PASS
[us-west-probe] 2025-03-18T12:14:22 FAIL code=timeout
[eu-probe] 2025-03-18T12:14:44 PASS
[us-east-probe] 2025-03-18T12:14:59 FAIL code=kv-miss
```
anya: ops-metrics: pod restarts are low, CPU fine. latency spikes align with route switch events. looks like healthcheck flapping not node OOM.
devon: I see policy churn in smart-router logs — a small rollout from yesterday added an aggressive cross-region fallback that prefers lower-cost variants. Might be choosing a variant that fails KV cache warmup and triggers healthchecks.
arnold: good catch. can we force sticky routing to last-known-good and freeze fallback policy? what's the `redwoodctl` command?
mikaela: run: `redwoodctl routing update --policy-id cross-region-fallback --freeze true` — that will stop automated fallback decisions while we triage. planning to route new traffic to last-stable variant in us-east.
arnold: executing now. `> redwoodctl routing update --policy-id cross-region-fallback --freeze true --auth @arnold`
ops-bot: routing policy cross-region-fallback set to FROZEN by arnold at 2025-03-18T12:22:05.
luis: after freeze, flip rate dropped immediately. 5xxs down from 30% to ~8% in 2 mins. still a handful of customers with degraded requests (orders-service, analytics-ingest).
sam-pd: notified account reps for affected customers: IDs 7123, 8199. told them we're mitigating and will follow up.
arnold: next step: identify model-variant differences. devon, can you dump the variant metadata for the routing candidates between us-east and us-west?
devon: pasted small diff: 
```
us-east-variant: model=v2.1 quant=8bit cache_warm=true init_seq=100
us-west-variant: model=v2.1 quant=8bit cache_warm=false init_seq=0  # KV cache disabled on startup
```
devon: us-west variant lacks KV warm initialization, so cold starts lead to failing quick health probes and immediate failover, which then warms other regions and causes the flip.
anya: mitigation plan: (1) continue freeze; (2) temporarily prefer pinned variant with cache_warm=true for routing table; (3) throttle probe frequency for 60s; (4) roll forward a fix to us-west variant to enable warm init.
arnold: implement step 2 now: `redwoodctl route set-preference --route default-text --candidate us-east-variant --priority 100`
ops-bot: route preference updated — default-text now prefers us-east-variant.
luis: metrics: probe failures drop to near zero after preference update. error budget burn stabilizing.
mikaela: I'm going to create a short-lived canary deploy to us-west with KV warm enabled. devon, please prepare image tag `v2.1-warm-20250318` and we'll push 2 pods to the us-west pool.
devon: pushing canary now. `kubectl apply -f canary-us-west.yaml` — canary up in 45s. logs show successful KV init.
arnold: monitoring for 5m. if stable, we'll unfreeze policy and revert pref to permissive.
incident-bot: advisory: customer-impact: partial degradation for small subset (IDs: 7123,8199). mitigation in progress.
anya: note for postmortem: runbook lacked explicit check for variant cache_warm settings; add a validation step to pre-deploy routing rules.
arnold: can we run an automated audit to find other regions with cache_warm=false for same model?
devon: running quick query: `redwoodctl models list --filter "model=v2.1" --fields region,variant,cache_warm` — results show eu variant also had cache_warm=false. I'll open a patch.
ops-bot: canary in us-west reports healthy for 10m, no probe flips observed.
luis: rolling back the routing preference to default permissive now that canary is good and I've increased probe debounce to 45s. `redwoodctl routing update --policy-id cross-region-fallback --freeze false`
ops-bot: cross-region-fallback policy unfrozen by luis at 2025-03-18T12:45:01.
arnold: confirm: traffic stable, 5xxs <1% system-wide, affected customers recovering. good work. I'll escalate to oncall follow-up and schedule postmortem doc.
mikaela: filed postmortem ticket: PM-4672, and added immediate action items: (a) add variant cache warm validation in rollout CI, (b) add routing policy guardrail to not prefer variants with cache_warm=false, (c) adjust probe debounce default.
sam-pd: sent customer follow-ups with mitigation summary and ETA for a permanent fix.
arnold: final — incident closed for paging. follow-ups assigned. thanks all. :tada:
